items.title: Who Is Using Pornography Generated by Artificial Intelligence? Correlates of AI-Porn Use and Familiarity in an Australian Adult Sample
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are rapidly transforming how people create and experience sexual content, including the emergence of AI-generated pornography (AI-porn). Yet little is known about who is engaging with this evolving medium. This study presents findings from a cross-sectional survey (data collected in 2025) of 367 heterosexual Australian adults (age range = 19–87 years, M = 39.07, SD = 13.43; 52.5% men, 44.8% women [and 2.2% non-binary, excluded from inferential analyses due to small cell sizes]) examining demographic, ideological, and relational correlates of AI-porn familiarity and use. Overall, 26.0% of participants reported having used AI-porn and were moderately familiar with it. Regression analyses showed that men and younger participants were significantly more likely to be familiar with and to have used AI-porn. Ideological factors (religiosity, political orientation) and relational factors (relationship status, relationship and sexual satisfaction) were not associated with use. These findings suggest that engagement with AI-porn is emerging most prominently among digitally curious younger men, yet appears ideologically broad and not linked (in this data set) to relationship dissatisfaction. As AI tools enable new forms of personalized, creative sexual expression, understanding who is exploring these technologies can help researchers and clinicians track evolving norms around intimacy, fantasy, and sexual media in the digital age.

items.title: Why Agentic Workflows Fail: A Taxonomy Derived from Literature and Empirical Data
items.abstract: Agentic workflows combine large language models with planning, memory, tools, execution environments, and iterative feedback. Their failures are difficult to diagnose because the same user-visible symptom may originate from model behavior, workflow orchestration, external tools, infrastructure, or their interaction. This paper presents a source-aware taxonomy of agentic workflow failures and applies it to evidence from academic literature and GitHub. The taxonomy combines source attribution with three empirical dimensions: a concrete failure-type dictionary, workflow-stage localization, and agent-capability localization. Its central structure is a two-axis localization matrix: workflow stages form the horizontal process axis and agent capabilities form the vertical functional axis. This design moves beyond taxonomies that mainly classify final failure manifestations by localizing intermediate process states inside agent operation. Our empirical comparison shows that literature-derived failures emphasize planning, reasoning, learning, perception, and knowledge-related mechanisms, whereas GitHub-derived failures concentrate on execution-stage, actuation-related, tool, API, and infrastructure failures. The dominant hotspot is iterative execution and actuation. These findings indicate that agentic workflow reliability should be treated as a systems problem rather than only a model-output problem. The taxonomy provides a basis for structured evaluation, root cause analysis, failure injection, and engineering triage.

items.title: Why disaster experience does not always improve Preparedness: The role of disaster learning and heterogeneous effects
items.abstract: The frequency and severity of natural disasters and public emergencies have continued to increase worldwide. Household preparedness plays a vital role in disaster risk reduction, yet the effect of disaster-related experience on preparedness remains inconclusive. Using survey data from 5,862 residents in China, this study separately examines the associations of past disaster experience and disaster learning with household preparedness. Conventional regression models and a causal forest approach are used to estimate average associations and explore heterogeneous effects across individuals. The results show that disaster learning, rather than past disaster experience, is positively associated with preparedness behavior, highlighting the importance of capacity building. In addition, both past disaster experience and disaster learning exhibit heterogeneous effects across individuals. Feature importance analysis further indicates that social capital, emergency awareness, and community infrastructure are important influential factors associated with preparedness behavior. By introducing a causal forest approach to distinguish the differential effects of past disaster experience and disaster learning, this study provides a more nuanced understanding of household preparedness and offers useful insights for developing more targeted household disaster risk reduction strategies.

items.title: Why Secure AI Adoption Is a Board-Level Priority
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from isolated experimentation into everyday enterprise workflows, knowledge repositories, business applications, and increasingly agentic systems. This paper argues that secure AI adoption should be treated as an enterprise governance and business-risk issue rather than as a narrowly scoped information-technology project. It proposes the Five Pillars of Secure AI Adoption, an author-developed framework comprising governance and accountability, data protection, identity and least privilege, AI-specific security controls, and monitoring and incident response. The framework provides an executive-oriented operating model informed by established resources, including the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the NIST Generative AI Profile, ISO/IEC 42001, and OWASP guidance for large-language-model and generative-AI application security. The paper concludes that security should enable responsible AI innovation through explicit ownership, controlled access, bounded agency, AI-aware safeguards, and observable operations.

items.title: Work-Related musculoskeletal disorders, burnout, and job satisfaction in physiotherapy technicians
items.abstract: BackgroundPhysiotherapy technicians are frequently exposed to heavy workloads and high patient volumes, which can lead to physical and emotional strain. Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) and burnout are common among healthcare workers and may negatively impact job satisfaction and overall occupational health. Data specifically addressing physiotherapy technicians, however, remain limited.ObjectiveTo examine the prevalence of WMSDs, burnout, and job satisfaction among physiotherapy technicians working in public and private hospitals.MethodsThis observational study was conducted between April 2025 and March 2026. A total of 122 physiotherapy technicians employed in public and private hospitals in Istanbul were included. Demographic data were recorded. The Extended Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire assessed musculoskeletal disorders, the Maslach Burnout Inventory evaluated burnout, and the Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire measured job satisfaction. Differences between groups and correlations among the study variables were analyzed.ResultsMusculoskeletal pain at any point in life was reported by 91.8% of participants, most commonly in the neck, lower back, and upper back. Musculoskeletal disorder scores were negatively correlated with job satisfaction and positively correlated with emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and total burnout scores. Strong negative correlations were observed between job satisfaction and burnout subdimensions. Technicians in private hospitals had lower job satisfaction and higher emotional exhaustion and depersonalization scores than those in public hospitals.ConclusionsWMSDs are highly prevalent among physiotherapy technicians and are significantly associated with increased burnout and reduced job satisfaction. Implementing workplace ergonomic interventions, improving working conditions, and providing ergonomics training are essential to protect employee health and enhance work performance.

items.title: WORKPLACE ENVIRONMENTAL PRACTICES AND EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE IN PUBLIC HEALTH SECTOR IN MACHAKOS COUNTY
items.abstract: The general objective of the study was to establish the effect of workplace environmental practices on employee performance in the Public Health Sector at Machakos County. It adopted a descriptive correlational research design and utilized a structured questionnaire as the primary instrument for data collection. The unit of analysis comprised Level 4 and Level 5 public health facilities in Machakos County. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods were used to examine the data using SPSS Version 29. While inferential analysis employed correlation and multiple regression techniques to look at the connections between the research variables, descriptive statistics, such as frequencies and percentages, were used to characterize demographic information. The results showed that employee performance was positively and significantly correlated with each of the independent factors. The psychosocial work environment (r = 0.52, p < 0.05), the physical work environment (r = 0.38, p < 0.05), organizational culture (r = 0.20, p < 0.05), and leadership style (r = 0.64, p < 0.05) showed the largest positive correlation with employee performance. Based on these results, the study came to the conclusion that organizational culture, psychological work environment, physical work environment, and leadership style all have a major impact on worker performance in Machakos County's public health sector. The research recommends that the public health sector in Machakos County invest in ergonomic equipment and comfortable workplace furniture to improve employee productivity. It also emphasizes the need for leaders to cultivate a collaborative work environment, encourage innovation, and adopt coaching, mentoring, and continuous training initiatives to enhance employee growth and performance. Key words: Workplace Environmental Practices, Employee Performance, Public Health Sector

items.title: WP-AI-8.4: The Capability-Safety-Responsibility Alignment Framework
items.abstract: WP-AI-8.4 develops a Capability-Safety-Responsibility Alignment Framework for governing the release of advanced AI systems into society. The paper begins from a structural distinction: capability advancement and social release are not the same governance question. Scientific and engineering progress determines what AI can do; governance must separately determine what capabilities may enter society, under what safety conditions, through whose authority, and with what responsibility attached. The framework argues that capability growth does not itself create a right to release. Social release should be justified by necessity, demonstrated governability, appropriate safety conditions, and an identifiable responsibility structure. Release is treated as a graduated and reversible process rather than a one-time product event, and material capability expansion after deployment is defined as a form of capability creep that should trigger renewed review. The paper further proposes that release boundaries should be defined by real-world exposure rather than by labels such as testing, evaluation, or experimentation. Where high-risk systems require realistic testing, the paper introduces the concept of a high-fidelity isolated “Shadow World” in which relevant real-world complexity can be reproduced without exposing the open world to uncontrolled experimental consequences. Drawing on the governance logic used in high-consequence technologies such as nuclear systems, the framework emphasizes staged safety review, staged authorization, cumulative responsibility, and legal accountability across the development, approval, deployment, configuration, and operational chain. It also introduces a non-propagation responsibility: organizations deploying generative AI should be responsible for ensuring that failures within their own controlled environment do not propagate into external networks, other institutions, unrelated users, or society. WP-AI-8.4 builds on the preceding papers in the WP-AI-8 series. WP-AI-8.1 established the engineering circuit-breaker principle; WP-AI-8.2 examined responsibility escape; WP-AI-8.3 connected capability control and human responsibility through a dual-track governance framework. WP-AI-8.4 extends this architecture to the release boundary itself, asking when and under what conditions AI capability may move from controlled development into social deployment.

items.title: XAI-Guided Fourier Domain Generalisation for Pure-Simulation Sim-to-Real Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning has shown strong potential for vision-based autonomous driving, but policies trained in simulation often suffer severe performance degradation when deployed in the real world. Existing sim-to-real methods commonly address this gap through image-transfer-based domain adaptation or policy-agnostic domain randomisation. However, the former requires laborious acquisition of target-domain data and is often limited to the deployment domain, whereas the latter introduces unguided perturbations that may not reflect the underlying sim-to-real discrepancy, leading to suboptimal transfer performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose XFD, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-guided Fourier domain generalisation framework for pure-simulation sim-to-real reinforcement learning. The proposed framework extracts explainability attribution maps from simulated observations, and converts these attributions into policy-conditioned Fourier-domain interventions. By perturbing appearance-sensitive spectral components while preserving task-defining spatial structures, XFD constructs robustness-enhancing visual domains entirely within simulation. Subsequently, the proposed robust policy optimisation guides the policy towards attending to task-critical features while suppressing sensitivity to irrelevant visual information. Extensive experiments in simulation and zero-shot real-world deployment demonstrate that XFD consistently improves traveled distance and reward over standard policy and randomly domain-randomised baseline, especially on unseen maps with cluttered backgrounds. Attribution-based analysis further proves that the proposed policy preserves more consistent task-relevant visual evidence across simulation and real-world observations.

items.abstract: The article provides a comprehensive examination of the evolution of theoretical approaches to innovation management and identifies the major directions in the transformation of its conceptual foundations under the influence of economic, technological, organizational, and societal changes. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that, in an increasingly dynamic competitive environment, characterized by digital transformation, the spread of open innovation, the development of innovation ecosystems, platform-based business models, and artificial intelligence, traditional approaches to managing innovation activities require substantial reconsideration. The evolution of academic thought demonstrates a gradual shift from viewing innovation primarily as the outcome of a firm's internal research and technological development activities toward understanding it as a complex, systemic process of creating, disseminating, and commercializing new knowledge, technologies, products, services, processes, and business models involving multiple actors within an innovation ecosystem. he purpose of the study is to systematize and generalize the main stages in the evolution of innovation management theories, identify the underlying logic of the transformation of relevant theoretical paradigms, and substantiate the specific features of the contemporary stage of innovation management development, which is characterized by openness, ecosystem-based interaction, digitalization, the development of dynamic capabilities, and the use of artificial intelligence. The methodological foundation of the study comprises a combination of general scientific and specialized research methods. The historical and logical method was used to identify the sequence of formation and transformation of innovation management theories; the methods of analysis and synthesis were applied to systematize the principles of contemporary theoretical concepts; the comparative method was used to identify the common and distinctive characteristics of the principal paradigms; the systems approach was employed to examine the interrelationships between innovation strategy, resources, organizational capabilities, innovation processes, external partners, and ecosystems; and the generalization method was used to develop an integrated understanding of the contemporary innovation management model. The theoretical and informational basis of the study comprises recent academic works by international and Ukrainian scholars addressing innovation management, open innovation, dynamic capabilities, innovation ecosystems, digital technologies, business model innovation, and artificial intelligence. The scientific novelty of the study lies in systematizing the evolution of innovation management theories as a successive transition from resource- and technology-based and linear models to process-based, capability-based, open, ecosystem, digital, and human–AI hybrid paradigms. These concepts are interpreted not as mutually exclusive approaches, but as interconnected stages in the expansion of the subject matter and scope of innovation management. The study substantiates that the contemporary transformation of innovation management is manifested in a shift from managing individual innovation projects toward developing and enhancing a firm's innovation capabilities, managing knowledge and partnership networks, and orchestrating innovation ecosystems. It is demonstrated that digitalization and artificial intelligence constitute a qualitatively new stage in the development of innovation management theory, in which innovation processes increasingly take the form of human–machine hybrid systems. The study identifies the principal patterns underlying the development of theoretical approaches to innovation management. It is established that the initial focus on technological resources, research and development has gradually been complemented by process-based approaches, the concept of dynamic organizational capabilities, open innovation, innovation ecosystems, and digital transformation. The findings demonstrate that contemporary innovation management encompasses not only the creation of new products and technologies but also the management of knowledge, organizational change, business models, partnership networks, digital data, and intelligent technologies. The principal stages of theoretical evolution are systematized according to the object of management, sources of innovation, the role of the firm, and mechanisms of value creation. The study substantiates the need to integrate process-based, strategic, resource-based, network, ecosystem, and digital approaches into a contemporary innovation management model. It is established that the future development of innovation management theory is associated with the formation of responsible innovation management models, the integration of human and artificial intelligence, the development of digital innovation ecosystems, and the increasing importance of firms' dynamic capabilities. The findings can be used to further develop the theoretical and methodological foundations of innovation management, formulate innovation strategies, and design practical mechanisms for strengthening firms' innovation capabilities.

items.abstract: The article examines the theoretical and practical principles of the functioning of e-commerce enterprises in service markets under the conditions of digital transformation of the economy. The essence of service e-commerce is defined, its specific features are identified, and the main types of services that can act as independent objects of electronic purchase and sale are systematized. Particular attention is paid to the characteristics that distinguish e-commerce in services from electronic trade in tangible goods, including the intangibility of services, the simultaneity of production and consumption, the impossibility of storing unused capacity, personalization, the global nature of digital interaction, and the critical role of digital platforms. The study systematizes the main risks faced by e-commerce enterprises, including cyber, technological, legal, reputational, financial, competitive, marketing, and operational risks. The economic specificity of service e-commerce is associated with the combination of service intangibility, the decisive role of digital platforms as an environment for interaction, and a high level of information asymmetry between sellers and consumers. The importance of mechanisms for preliminary verification of service providers, standardization of service quality criteria and contractual conditions, payment and personal data protection, documentation of service delivery, guarantees, and alternative dispute resolution is substantiated. The study also emphasizes the importance of customer trust, transparency of digital transactions, and the availability of reliable feedback mechanisms, which directly affect consumer decision-making and the long-term sustainability of service providers in digital markets. It is concluded that the efficiency and competitiveness of e-commerce enterprises depend on their digital maturity, management quality, adaptability, and ability to implement innovative technologies. Further development is associated with artificial intelligence, business process automation, and the creation of integrated digital ecosystems.

items.abstract: The article substantiates the role of innovative management tools as a lever for the development of product IT companies under conditions of environmental turbulence, shortening digital product life cycles and intensifying global competition for users and for qualified specialists. It is shown that a product IT company constitutes a specific object of management, characterised by a high share of intangible assets, the transfer of market demand risk to the company itself, the network nature of value and a critical dependence of results on the quality of managerial decisions rather than on the volume of resources involved. Consequently, the traditional lever of growth, namely the accumulation of resources, demonstrates sharply diminishing returns, whereas the returns on the managerial lever increase. The paper clarifies the content of the concept of an innovative management tool, defined as a formalised and reproducible means of influencing the management system that changes the mechanism of decision-making, resource allocation or coordination and provides a measurable increase in organisational adaptability. A five-element classification is developed according to functional purpose, covering tools of strategic goal-setting and alignment, organisational and process tools, product discovery tools, analytical and measurement tools, and human-centred tools including digital and artificial intelligence solutions. A lever model is proposed that explains the conversion of a managerial innovation into growth of company value through four transmission links: shortening of the feedback loop, an increase in the share of validated decisions, growth of value-stream throughput and retention of key competence. A methodological approach to evaluating implementation performance is grounded on an integral index that aggregates five groups of partial indicators using minimax normalisation and expert weighting, accompanied by an interpretation scale distinguishing imitative, fragmentary and systemic implementation. The correspondence between tools and the stages of a company life cycle is established, and barriers to implementation in the Ukrainian context are identified.

items.abstract: The article substantiates the conceptual foundations for forming a digital security ecosystem in the tourism and hospitality industry. It is established that the digital transformation of tourism and hospitality enterprises and the spread of online booking platforms, mobile services, artificial intelligence, geographic information systems, the Internet of Things and cloud technologies simultaneously expand safety management capabilities and create new cyber, information, operational and reputational risks. The concept of a «digital security ecosystem in the tourism and hospitality industry» is clarified as an integrated human-centred environment for interaction among tourists, enterprises, digital platforms, public authorities, insurance and financial institutions, and emergency services, within which continuous data exchange, monitoring, forecasting, prevention, localisation and risk minimisation are ensured at all stages of the tourist journey. The main groups of threats are systematised, and the stakeholder, information, technological, functional and institutional components of the ecosystem are identified. The author’s Digital Security Ecosystem for Tourism and Hospitality (DSETH-model) is proposed, combining digital identification, data integration, risk monitoring, predictive analytics, communication, response and recovery. The principles of its functioning are substantiated: integration, interoperability, prevention, continuity, adaptability, cyber resilience, confidentiality, reliability, inclusiveness and accountability. The stages of practical ecosystem implementation and a set of indicators for assessing its effectiveness are determined. Particular attention is paid to the integration of digital technologies into a unified security environment capable of supporting proactive risk management and improving coordination among all stakeholders. The proposed conceptual framework may serve as a methodological basis for developing digital security strategies and implementing innovative management solutions in the tourism and hospitality industry. It is proved that applying an ecosystem approach will help reduce threat response time, increase consumer trust, strengthen the resilience of enterprises and tourism destinations, improve service quality and enhance the competitiveness of the tourism and hospitality industry.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence adoption is expanding across the European Union, while national averages conceal substantial firm-size differences. Absolute and relative gaps describe different dimensions of this diffusion. The paper examines cross-country and firm-size inequality in AI adoption across all 27 EU Member States and distinguishes absolute distance from proportional disadvantage. The empirical base is Eurostat’s 2026 statistical report with 2025 country-by-size adoption rates. The absolute gap is the large-enterprise rate minus the small-enterprise rate; the normalised gap divides this difference by their sum. Spearman rank correlations are primary and Pearson coefficients supplementary. Because the official all-enterprise rate is size-weighted and correlates almost perfectly with small-enterprise adoption, relative-gap inference relies mainly on an equal-weight measure averaging small, medium and large enterprises. A medium-enterprise-only correlation provides a check independent of the normalised-gap formula. Coefficients of variation use the population standard deviation for the complete set of 27 Member States. AI was used by 17.0% of small and 55.0% of large EU enterprises. Small-enterprise adoption ranged from 4.1% to 37.5% across countries (CV=0.515), compared with 20.8% to 79.4% among large enterprises (CV=0.274). The national adoption rate is moderately positively associated with the absolute gap (Spearman ρ=0.477, p=0.012). The equal-weight measure is strongly negatively associated with the normalised gap (ρ=−0.816, p<0.001), and the medium-enterprise check is even stronger (ρ=−0.846, p<0.001). Among non-users, only 12.7% of small enterprises had considered AI adoption, compared with 36.5% of large enterprises; reported implementation barriers differed much less across size classes. Cross-country relative dispersion is substantially greater among small enterprises. A higher size-standardised adoption level can coexist with a sizeable absolute large-small distance while being associated with a markedly smaller proportional disadvantage of small firms. The results are cross-sectional associations based on published Eurostat point estimates and do not establish causality.

items.abstract: The article examines the transformation of the advertising services market within the e-business ecosystem, emphasizing the contradictory influence of global economic fragmentation and sustainable development imperatives. It is shown that the digitalization of advertising, the platformization of e-business, the diffusion of algorithmic technologies and artificial intelligence are reshaping interactions among advertisers, digital platforms and e-consumers and changing the mechanisms of creating, distributing and evaluating advertising value. The study argues that the technological globalization of advertising increasingly coexists with institutional, regulatory, technological and data fragmentation of the digital environment. This combination creates a fundamentally new configuration of the global advertising market, in which the growing technological interconnectedness of market participants is accompanied by increasing differentiation of regulatory regimes, digital ecosystems and conditions for accessing consumer data. Particular attention is paid to the growing concentration of platforms and investment resources, the regional differentiation of data governance rules, and the increasing role of AI-driven advertising, retail media and programmatic technologies. It is emphasized that these processes strengthen the role of data, algorithms and digital infrastructure as strategic resources of advertising activities and simultaneously increase the dependence of e-business entities on technological platforms and their ecosystems. Sustainable development is considered not only as a communication agenda but as a criterion for organizing advertising production and delivery, including responsible data use, carbon efficiency, algorithmic transparency, inclusiveness and consumer trust. In this context, the transformation of advertising efficiency criteria is substantiated, as economic performance is increasingly complemented by environmental, technological, ethical and social dimensions. The article develops an original transformation matrix and a conceptual model linking global fragmentation, digital platforms, data, algorithms, sustainable development and the transformation of e-business. The proposed approach makes it possible to interpret the contemporary advertising services market as a complex platform-algorithmic ecosystem whose development is determined by the interaction of technological, economic, institutional, environmental and behavioral factors. Four scenarios for the advertising services market up to 2030 are outlined: inertial, fragmentation-based, platform-algorithmic and sustainable-adaptive. The sustainable-adaptive scenario is identified as the most balanced trajectory for the long-term development of the advertising services market and e-business ecosystem. It is concluded that the advertising market is moving from an economy of advertising reach toward an economy of algorithmically managed, adaptive and responsible interaction with consumers, in which technological efficiency, strategic adaptability and responsible sustainability become interconnected determinants of long-term competitiveness.

items.abstract: This document, S15. Observations on the Fundamentals of Aesthetic Cognition, belongs to the Five Ways · One Law knowledge repository, categorized under observational records (ShiBu). The text only documents observable phenomena, presuppositions and unresolved open questions about human aesthetic perception. The observation covers multiple dimensions: Contrast between continuous natural aesthetic ontology and discretized, standardized man-made representations under industrialization, market economy and educational indoctrination; Prerequisites for delicate aesthetic contemplation: mental quietude, cognitive knowledge support and release from urgent survival pressure; Correlation between survival anxiety and the capacity for fine aesthetic observation, illustrated through selected historical cases, with explicit caveats that these are partial examples without universal generalization; Distinction between extrinsic objective aesthetic stimuli (subject to biological sensory fatigue) and intrinsic subjective aesthetic experience (cumulative and growing); Two-layer mechanism for human beauty judgment: innate perceptual instinct and acquired learned evaluation criteria. The manuscript puts forward an open proposition: aesthetic cultivation relies on quietude for contemplation, knowledge for reflective thinking, authenticity to restrain illusory perception, and relaxed non-survival-oriented mental space to nurture endogenous aesthetic sensibility. All statements are reserved as open-ended observations. The complete formation mechanism of aesthetic perception remains undetermined for further continued observation. items.abstract: The emergence of Generation Z has coincided with major changes in education, communication, technology and social life. Students of this generation learn in an environment shaped by smartphones, social media, digital platforms, online resources and increasingly, generative artificial intelligence (AI). These developments have expanded access to information and created opportunities for personalized and innovative learning, but have also introduced challenges such as distraction, information overload, social comparison, digital well-being concerns and academic pressure. The present paper examines the educational implications of Generation Z in relation to digital culture, educational innovation and social transformation, while drawing upon an earlier empirical study of anxiety and academic achievement among 400 XII-grade students in Jamshedpur. The sample consisted of 200 Arts and 200 Science students preparing for the ISC Board Examination. Anxiety was examined through Examination, Social, Personal and Family Anxiety, while academic achievement was assessed through pre-board examination marks. The findings indicate predominantly moderate anxiety in both groups. No significant differences were found between Arts and Science students in Examination and Social Anxiety, whereas significant differences were found in Personal and Family Anxiety. A significant difference was also reported in academic achievement, with Arts students obtaining a higher mean score than Science students. The paper reinterprets these findings in the contemporary context of Generation Z without claiming that digital technology caused the reported anxiety. items.title: “It Works, but I Don’t Know Why”: Uncritical Use, Verification Behavior and Perceived Understanding in Non-CS Students’ Generative AI-Assisted Programming Projects
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) enables students with little programming experience to produce working software, raising the concern that learners may build artifacts they cannot explain. This convergent mixed-methods study examined how uncritical GenAI use and verification behavior (VB) relate to novices’ self-reported understanding of their own AI-assisted projects. Participants were undergraduates from predominantly non-computing majors in two offerings of a general-education Python course; 64 provided complete survey data and 68 written reflections were thematically analyzed. Uncritical use (UR) was associated with a larger self-reported product–understanding gap (GAP; r = 0.43, p < 0.001) but showed little association with perceived understanding (PU), whereas VB was associated with PU (r = 0.45, p < 0.001) but showed little association with the gap. Tests of dependent correlations confirmed that these associations differed. In the reflections, execution-based checking was the most commonly reported verification strategy (47 of 68), whereas comprehension-oriented strategies were less common. Because all measures were self-reported and cross-sectional, the findings are correlational; they suggest that instruction should explicitly scaffold comprehension-oriented verification in AI-integrated introductory programming.

items.title: "Role of Digital Education Innovation in Building a Technologically Literate Society: A Conceptual Study with Reference to Generation Z Students"
items.abstract: In the twenty-first century, digital technology brought about extensive changes in the nature, process, and objectives of education. Moving beyond traditional teacher-centered and classroom-centered teaching, education is now advancing towards online learning, blended learning, smart classrooms, mobile learning, digital teaching resources, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based teaching. In this context, Generation Z students are particularly important because their social and educational environment has developed alongside digital technologies. Technological media has made the teaching-learning process more flexible, participatory, and student-centered. Generation Z is the generation that has grown up with digital technologies. Thus, digital education innovation is not merely a means of modernizing the teaching process; it is also an important means of developing technological literacy among students. The objective of this conceptual research paper is to clarify the conceptual relationship between digital education innovation and technological literacy with reference to Generation Z students. In this study, digital education innovation is viewed as an educational process in which digital devices, online teaching, AI-based technologies, digital resources, and innovative teaching methods are effectively used. Technological literacy refers to students’ ability to understand, use, evaluate, and to employ technological devices and digital resources safely and responsibly. This paper argues that effective digital education innovation can provide a strong foundation for students’ technological competence, digital problem-solving ability, information evaluation ability, and digital citizenship. At the same time, it is necessary to pay attention to challenges such as the digital divide, technological inequality, digital safety, teacher training, availability of technological resources, misinformation, privacy, cybersecurity, and uncontrolled use of artificial intelligence.

items.title: $Δ$ Flow Matching for Robot Foundation Models
items.abstract: Flow matching is a common generative recipe for robot foundation models. Vision-language-action models (VLAs) generate action chunks, while world-action models (WAMs) additionally generate future visual states. Both start generation from a fixed Gaussian prior, despite temporal continuity between past and future states and actions. This requires costly training and iterative sampling, especially for WAMs with an additional visual branch. We introduce $Δ$-flow, which constructs the source from recent history with mild noise rather than from a fixed Gaussian prior. This moves the source closer to the target, reducing transport to a small residual $Δ$ that can be learned efficiently and enables single-step inference. We integrate $Δ$-flow into the VLA policy $π_{0.5}$ and the WAM policies ImageWAM and Fast-WAM. On LIBERO, ImageWAM reaches 90% success in one epoch rather than six, and Fast-WAM reaches 95% in two epochs rather than eight. With LoRA fine-tuning, $π_{0.5}$ exceeds its baseline's five-epoch performance after one epoch. Single-step inference gives $1.54\times$, $2.49\times$, and $4.45\times$ speedups on $π_{0.5}$, ImageWAM, and Fast-WAM, respectively. It preserves action smoothness, achieving a $4.5\times$ reduction in action jerk compared with one-step Gaussian sampling. $Δ$-flow reaches state-of-the-art generalization performance on LIBERO-Plus. Action-history sources can be applied to pretrained WAM policies without retraining. Replacing the Gaussian action source at inference largely preserves task success with a single sampling step and can slightly improve it. We further study how action representation and visual information in action learning affect history-to-future prediction in $Δ$-flow. These results show that $Δ$-flow is simple yet effective, improving the efficiency and generalization of robot foundation models.

items.title: A COMPARATIVE EVIDENCE-BASED ASSESSMENT OF TRAINING-SIMULATOR SOFTWARE AND HARDWARE: A MODULAR, HUMAN-CENTRED RESEARCH FRAMEWORK IN THE QW-18 CONTEXT
items.abstract: This article presents a comparative analysis of existing software and hardware solutions used in training simulators for man-portable air-defense system operators. The study examines the main features of the Stinger Simulator, I-STPTv2, Igla-2 Trainer, and 9F635M1 field simulator based on available technical information. Particular attention is given to simulator functionality, instructor control, virtual environments, data collection, performance assessment, and system flexibility. Based on the comparative analysis, a modular intelligent training simulator architecture for the QW-18 system is proposed. The proposed architecture consists of six interconnected functional modules organized into three main layers. The study also considers the potential application of artificial intelligence for analyzing training results and supporting individual learning. The proposed approach provides a theoretical and methodological basis for the further development and evaluation of modern training simulators.

items.title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
items.abstract: Large language model agents are emerging as an important new class of users of desktop applications. However, existing desktop interfaces were designed for human end users or application developers, leaving agents to interpret visual controls or discover and compose low-level software operations. This mismatch can hinder even capable agents, yet it remains unclear what interface properties make desktop software easier for agents to use. To study this question, we treat software evolution as a natural source of interface variation and introduce DeskIF-Bench, a benchmark of 255 artifact-verified tasks across six desktop applications. By holding the task, agent, and verifier fixed while varying the software release, we measure how interface changes affect agent performance. Across two models and six applications, the newest release consistently outperforms the oldest. Trajectory analysis identifies three relevant interface properties: discoverability, granularity, and observability. Guided by these properties, we develop ANIS, a framework that synthesizes agent-native interfaces from the capabilities of installed applications. On an expanded evaluation of 368 tasks across eight applications, atomic interfaces improve success over native SDK use by 3.8 and 3.5 percentage points with DeepSeek V4 Flash and Claude Haiku 4.5, respectively, while reducing online token usage by approximately 73%. Goal-level commands further raise success to 74.5% and 67.4%, respectively.

items.title: A Fuzzy Multi-Criteria Decision Framework with Ant Colony Optimization and Adaptive Inference for Personalized Route Recommendation: A Museum Guidance Case Study
items.abstract: Personalized recommendation under uncertain user preferences and conflicting multi-criteria constraints poses a fundamental challenge in decision support systems. This study proposes a framework integrating fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making (FMCDM) with ant colony optimization (ACO). The framework contributes three components: a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference engine transforming linguistic preferences into priority scores across four criteria; an FMCDM-enhanced ACO algorithm embedding fuzzy scoring into transition probabilities for route optimization; and an adaptive inference mechanism recalibrating recommendation depth based on behavioral signals. The framework is evaluated through Monte Carlo simulation using the Rijksmuseum dataset (60 artifacts). Simulation across 7500 synthetic trajectories suggests 15.5% higher path efficiency than TOPSIS-based baselines under modeled conditions (criteria balance SD: 0.033 vs. 0.171). A preliminary expert assessment with twelve museum professionals (N = 12) provides exploratory evidence that human–AI collaborative content approaches human-authored quality at substantially reduced production time.

items.title: A multi-model LLM framework for AI-assisted psychological scale development: initial psychometric evaluation of the Emotion Regulation Scale (ERS)
items.abstract: Emotion regulation is a key construct in mental health, yet existing measures differ in conceptual coverage, with some focusing on specific strategies or regulatory difficulties rather than broader cognitive, behavioral, and contextual regulation processes. This study aimed to develop an Emotion Regulation Scale (ERS) grounded in Gross’s Process Model, using large language models (LLMs) as assistive tools within an established psychometric framework. This cross-sectional study included 743 adults recruited through convenience sampling. Participants were randomly divided into two non-overlapping subsamples, one used for exploratory factor analysis and the other for confirmatory factor analysis. Multiple LLMs and AI-based tools assisted with item generation, refinement and bias screening, translation, and post-EFA construct interpretation, with human oversight throughout development. An initial pool of 25 items was generated and refined to produce the final 17-item ERS. The ERS revealed a preliminary four-factor structure, with EFA explaining 50.85% of the variance. CFA provided preliminary support for a post hoc refined 17-item model (χ²/df = 1.95, CFI = 0.934, TLI = 0.918, IFI = 0.935, RMSEA = 0.050). Reliability was acceptable for early-stage scale development (α = 0.68–0.74; ω = 0.68–0.75). Convergent validity showed positive correlations between adaptive strategies and cognitive reappraisal ( r = 0.522–0.608) and between maladaptive cognitions and suppression ( r = 0.400). Concurrent validity showed associations with depression ( r = 0.432), anxiety ( r = 0.462), well-being ( r = -0.330), and quality of life (QOL1 = -0.357; QOL2 = -0.295), while adaptive strategies correlated with depression ( r = -0.184 to -0.239), anxiety ( r = -0.141 to -0.211), well-being ( r = 0.150 to 0.203), and quality of life ( r = 0.211 to 0.375). Known-groups validity indicated significant differences across depression and anxiety levels (MCR: F(4, 738) = 39.32; 64.49, p < 0.001). The findings provide preliminary psychometric evidence for the 17-item ERS and suggest that it may complement existing measures by capturing broader cognitive, behavioral, and contextual emotion regulation processes. The study illustrates the potential for LLM-assisted scale development within established psychometric procedures and human oversight. Further research using diverse samples is needed to evaluate the scale’s psychometric properties, generalizability, and broader utility.

items.title: A narrative review of occupational and community acquired infections among healthcare workers including exposure routes risk factors and infection prevention and control strategies from 2015 to 2025
items.abstract: Abstract Healthcare workers (HCWs) face infection risks through patient care, specimen processing, sharps, contaminated environments, and exposures outside healthcare settings. Vulnerability was illustrated during COVID-19, when the World Health Organization estimated that 80,000–180,000 health and care workers could have died from COVID-19 between January 2020 and May 2021. This narrative review examines role-specific exposure pathways, barriers to adherence to infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, and strategies for reducing occupational and community-acquired infections among HCWs. English-language sources published during 2015–2025 were identified through targeted database and public-health-agency searches, last updated 30 June 2026. Evidence was organized thematically by HCW role, transmission route, barrier, and preventive intervention. Occupational risk was concentrated in aerosol-generating procedures, dental drilling, airway management, specimen centrifugation, direct contact with lesions or body fluids, sharps injuries, and contaminated equipment or surfaces. Recurrent barriers included inadequate training, personal protective equipment (PPE) shortages or poor fit, workload, staffing deficiencies, emergency time pressure, weak safety culture, and inconsistent institutional enforcement, with resource limitations especially influential in low- and middle-income settings. Community respiratory and household exposures may cause workforce infection and contribute to subsequent transmission within healthcare settings. Effective protection therefore requires standard precautions, transmission-based precautions, vaccination, safe sharps systems, engineering and environmental controls, adequate staffing, continuous competency-based training, and leadership accountability. Protecting HCWs should be treated as both an occupational-health obligation and a patient-safety strategy; interventions should be adapted to task-specific risks and local resources rather than relying on PPE alone.

items.title: A New Approach to Human Factors Management
items.abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to managing the human factor within an occupational safety management system. The approach is based on viewing the human factor as the interaction between two complex nonlinear dynamic systems: “human characteristics” and “working conditions.” The authors introduce a quantitative assessment of the human factor by comparing the worker’s actual set of abilities–intellectual, sensory, protective, and physical–with the required set of abilities determined by the working conditions. A model of a personal occupational safety management system has been developed. This system forms part of an individual’s self-management system and is responsible for preserving the worker’s life and health. A method for assessing the effectiveness of this system is also proposed, based on the difference between the actual and required abilities to manage personal occupational safety measures. Based on the proposed model, a technology for continuous rapid workplace training has been developed. It is aimed at forming sustainable safe-behavior skills among workers. The paper presents an analysis of the results of implementing this technology at industrial enterprises, which demonstrated a 1.5- to 3-fold reduction in occupational injuries over a period of one to two years. It was established that workers displaying a safe type of behavior experience occupational injuries eight times less frequently than those displaying unsafe behavior. The authors conclude that the proposed approach is highly effective in practice as a tool for the large-scale development of safe behavior.

items.title: A Persian Vision-Language-Action Dataset and Benchmark for Ambiguity- and Infeasibility-Aware Instruction-to-Plan Grounding
items.abstract: Converting natural-language instructions into executable action plans conditioned on a scene image is a core capability for embodied human-robot interaction, but existing benchmarks target English, simulated or video-grounded environments, and largely assume instructions are clear and executable. We introduce the first Persian vision-language-action dataset for this task: 258 instances over 230 real household/office photographs, annotated with reference plans, deliberate ambiguity and infeasibility labels, disambiguating question-answer pairs, and an auto-generated chain-of-thought rationale for training. Using this resource, we ablate retrieval-augmentation, chain-of-thought prompting, and an agentic disambiguation step, evaluated with an LLM-as-judge protocol and a new metric, PGOS-FA, extending prior work (PG2S) with step-order sensitivity, an over-generation penalty, and Persian-adapted embeddings. Paired statistical testing across 36 comparisons shows retrieval-augmentation is a large, robustly significant effect, while finer-grained additions are directionally consistent but not statistically distinguishable from noise at this scale, and the LLM-judge metric has near-zero power where PGOS-FA succeeds. A blind human-correlation study on 79 real outputs shows PGOS-FA tracks human judgment at least as closely as the LLM-judge. Testing generalization beyond the ablation's single backbone, we find that most of the gap between an open-weight and a substantially stronger closed planner is attributable to open-weight model generation rather than to the closed model's capability specifically, and that our best configuration significantly outperforms an independently reproduced external baseline despite a weaker backbone. The dataset, PGOS-FA implementation, and evaluation code will be made available upon reasonable request.

items.title: A Safety-Aware Agentic LLM–Digital Twin Framework for Fuzzy Multi-Objective Control of Industrial Fed-Batch Bioreactors
items.abstract: This study develops a safety-aware supervisory framework for industrial fed-batch bioreactors by integrating an adaptive digital twin, fuzzy multi-objective optimization, Agentic LLM reasoning, and an independent Safety Governor within a closed-loop architecture. The digital twin continuously reconstructs process states and updates sensitive parameters, while α-cut fuzzy intervals preserve biological and operational uncertainty throughout prediction and optimization. The Agentic LLM coordinates prediction, optimization, process knowledge, and candidate evaluation, and supports context-dependent reevaluation and replanning as operating conditions evolve. The framework was evaluated using data from 12 industrial 72 h fed-batch runs, together with 600 uncertainty-aware simulated trajectories. Across three fully independent validation batches, the digital twin achieved an average NRMSE of 4.7%, MAPE of 4.4%, and R2 of 0.985. Closed-loop operation achieved a volumetric productivity of 0.347 g/L·h while maintaining a positive minimum dissolved-oxygen margin of 5 percentage points and zero hard-constraint violations. Across nominal and stressed scenarios, the Safety Governor preserved feasible operation with no residual hard-constraint violations, while the Agentic LLM successfully activated reevaluation and replanning following changes in process conditions. The ablation results further showed that the complete architecture provided the strongest overall balance among productivity, biological risk, robustness, and disturbance recovery. These findings demonstrate the value of combining adaptive process representation, uncertainty-aware optimization, agentic supervisory reasoning, and independent safety validation for reliable intelligent bioprocess operation.

items.title: A Sequential Multi-Stage Framework for Electric Vehicle Charging Management Integrating Forecasting, Optimisation, and LLM-Based Explanation
items.abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) adoption grows, improving EV charging management depends on accurate forecasts of charging demand and station occupancy, along with effective route guidance and dynamic charging-selection policies. Yet many existing approaches address only one component and do not provide an end-to-end pipeline that handles multiple goals. To overcome this limitation, this study introduces a sequential, multi-stage framework that predicts EV charging volume and occupancy under dynamic conditions while simultaneously optimising objectives such as routing, congestion, and cost. For forecasting, the framework uses an LSTM–Transformer model to learn both local and global dependencies and to deliver multi-horizon predictions. For optimisation, it applies reinforcement learning with proximal policy optimisation (RL-PPO), improving decisions by utilising a predicted feature map. In addition, the forecasting signals and agent outputs are leveraged to produce interpretable, LLM-based explanations, helping users to better understand the model’s predictions. The framework is evaluated on diverse datasets, including urban networks from two public benchmarks (UrbanEV and Multi-Faceted) and custom data from the Al Jouf region in Saudi Arabia. The results demonstrate the model’s effectiveness, achieving minimum RMSE values of 0.3244, 0.9339, and 0.15, with predictions closely matching the observed signals. In the optimisation stage, the proposed RL-PPO method achieves the best performance across all three datasets in terms of distance (km), congestion, and waiting time, resulting in higher customer satisfaction and a stronger trade-off than competing methods. Overall, the study delivers accurate forecasting, optimised decision support, and human-readable explanations, enabling an intelligent EV charging system.

items.title: A Study on the Factors Associated with College Students’ Intention to Use AI-Based Mental Health Services: The Roles of Trust, Empathy, and Privacy Concern
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence technology is gradually being integrated into mental health service contexts and is increasingly discussed as a potential supplementary resource to university mental health support systems. However, AI-based mental health services involve sensitive factors such as emotional expression, personal privacy, and relational interaction. Therefore, college students’ willingness to accept AI-based mental health services and the potential factors associated with such acceptance remain unclear. Based on an extended Technology Acceptance Model, this study introduces six factors—Accessibility (ACC), Privacy Concern (PC), Perceived Anthropomorphism (PA), Perceived Empathy (EMP), Trust (TRU), and Perceived Usefulness (PU)—to systematically examine their relationships with university students’ Behavioral Intention (BI) to use AI-based mental health services. A total of 375 volunteers participated in the current study and completed relevant questionnaires. Structural equation modeling was employed for data analysis. The results indicate that accessibility, perceived usefulness, and trust are all significantly and positively associated with behavioral intention. Perceived empathy is significantly and positively associated with trust, whereas privacy concern is significantly and negatively associated with both trust and behavioral intention. The analysis of indirect effects shows that there is a significant sequential indirect association between perceived anthropomorphism and behavioral intention through perceived empathy, trust, and perceived usefulness. In addition, a significant negative indirect association between privacy concern and behavioral intention through trust was observed. The findings indicate that, in the highly sensitive context of mental health services, college students’ intention to use AI-based mental health services is associated with a combination of accessibility, perceived usefulness, emotional interaction experience, privacy-related evaluations, and trust.

items.title: A Study on Youth’s Awareness and Understanding of Data Privacy While Using AI Chatbots in Maharashtra.
items.abstract: The extensive usage of AI chatbots, such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini, has led to a complete transformation of the ways young people acquire information, conduct their academic assignments, and perform technical tasks. However, with the rise in popularity of these platforms, worries emerge regarding the protection of users' information while exchanging it on these sites. The purpose of this study is to identify the degree of awareness regarding the problem of data privacy among young people who use AI chatbots in the state of Maharashtra. The descriptive approach was applied in the research process, and primary data were collected through the use of Google Forms surveys. The sample consisted of 151 respondents aged 15-29 who utilized AI chatbots and exchanged personal information, privacy measures, risks, knowledge about the storage and training of the model, and data protection laws. Some of the AI systems that were in common usage include ChatGPT and Google Gemini, while the type of information that was in widespread sharing included academic information. However, there is one other important observation on the lack of privacy settings, the lack of awareness of storing conversations, and also the limited self-reported awareness of the Indian Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 or similar data laws. The findings of this research suggest the need for proper digital privacy education, clear privacy information in different languages, proper data sharing, and awareness programs.

items.title: Active Learning Strategies on Teacher Education Students’ Attitude and Level of Engagement
items.abstract: This study investigated the dynamics of student engagement within active learning environments, specifically analyzing the relationships between students' attitudes and their behavioral, emotional, and cognitive involvement. Utilizing quantitative research, particularly a descriptive-correlational research design, this study identified the levels of student engagement and evaluated its relationship with their attitude in active learning activities. Through complete enumeration sampling, 44 teacher education students were identified, and their responses were analyzed through weighted means and the Pearson (r) product-moment correlation coefficient. Findings revealed that students are "Highly Engaged" across all measured dimensions, with Grand Means for Behavioral (M=3.78), Emotional (M=3.84), and Cognitive Engagement (M=3.77) reflecting substantial student investment. Statistical analysis confirmed significant positive correlations (p < 0.001) between students' attitudes—notably their Willingness to Participate and Perceived Usefulness—and their engagement levels. Specifically, the strong correlation between Willingness to Participate and Cognitive Engagement (r = 0.79) suggested that students’ internal readiness is closely associated with metacognitive processing and deep learning. The study concluded that engagement may be understood as a dynamic and reciprocal system in which positive attitudes are strongly linked to meaningful learning processes. The practical implications suggest that educators should prioritize confidence-building, low-stakes activities, and structured peer-facilitation roles to help create a supportive classroom community. By fostering a positive “Attitude Filter,” instructors may enhance conditions that support student retention and academic mastery.

items.title: Adaptive Look, Flexible Thought: Learning How and How Long to Think in Multimodal Reasoning
items.abstract: The introduction of long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and external tools has substantially improved the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on general and reasoning tasks. However, existing fast-slow reasoning paradigms mainly regulate textual reasoning length, while visual computation introduced by external tools or visual tokens is often treated as an auxiliary component. This separation prevents MLLMs from jointly optimizing visual perception and textual reasoning. To address this issue, we propose L2T (adaptive Look, flexible Thought), a unified reasoning framework that jointly optimizes the form and depth of computation. L2T first discretizes tool-produced visual states into visual tokens, bringing visual perception and textual reasoning into a shared autoregressive space. Based on this unified representation, L2T introduces a modality-aware routing reward to select appropriate reasoning modes and a difficulty-aware fast-slow strategy to adapt reasoning depth according to task complexity. Experiments on general perception and reasoning-intensive tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of L2T. Compared with explicit tool-calling approaches, L2T maintains competitive performance while achieving 1.7--3.6 times higher throughput.

items.abstract: Hou-Hsun Liao,1– 3 Yu-Sheng Liu,1 Ying-To Hsu,4 Ming-Hsien Yeh,1 Szu-Chin Li,5,6 Tzung-Yi Tsai7,81Department of Chinese Medicine, Dalin Tzu Chi Hospital, Buddhist Tzu Chi Medical Foundation, Chiayi, Taiwan; 2Department of Biochemical Science and Technology, College of Life Sciences, National Chiayi University, Chiayi City, Taiwan; 3Master Program in Integrated Medicine and Pharmacy Science, College of Life Sciences, National Chiayi University, Chiayi City, Taiwan; 4Division of Allergy, Immunology and Rheumatology, Dalin Tzu Chi Hospital, Buddhist Tzu Chi Medical Foundation, Chiayi, Taiwan; 5School of Medicine, Tzu Chi University, Hualien, Taiwan; 6Division of Hematology and Oncology, Department of Internal Medicine, Dalin Tzu Chi Hospital, Buddhist Tzu Chi Medical Foundation, Chiayi, Taiwan; 7Department of Environmental and Occupational Health, College of Medicine, National Cheng Kung University, Tainan, Taiwan; 8Department of Medical Research, Dalin Tzu Chi Hospital, Buddhist Tzu Chi Medical Foundation, Chiayi, TaiwanCorrespondence: Szu-Chin Li; Tzung-Yi Tsai, Email lisrau@gmail.com; dm732024@tzuchi.com.twBackground: Systemic chemotherapy increases the risk of thrombocytopenia in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), which may lead to risk of bleeding and treatment interruption. Accumulating evidence indicates that traditional Chinese medicinal herbs (TCMH) may accelerate symptom relief. We hypothesized that integrating TCMH alongside standard treatment may decrease the risk of chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia (CIT) in patients with AML.Aim: To compare the likelihood of CIT among patients with AML who received adjunctive TCMH plus standard treatment and those who received standard treatment alone.Methods: This nested case–control study analyzed individuals aged 20 and older who were newly diagnosed with AML, had no pre-existing CIT, and were identified from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database between 2002 and 2010. Five controls were then randomly matched to each CIT case from the remaining eligible cohort. All participants were followed until December 31, 2013. Conditional logistic regression was used to assess the association between TCMH use and risk of developing CIT.Results: TCMH was prescribed in 5.5% of cases and 20.6% of controls. Combining TCMH treatment with standard therapy substantially reduced risk of CIT (OR= 0.21; 95% CI:0.11– 0.39). The inverse association between adjunctive TCMH use and CIT was strongest among patients who received TCMH for more than 180 days. Age and gender did not influence the association between TCMH use and the risk of CIT.Conclusion: The current research emphasized the importance of framing a collaborative healthcare model for AML persons, especially involvement of TCMH, to effectively manage the poor complications that arise from cancer therapy.Keywords: acute myeloid leukemia, chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia, traditional Chinese medicinal herbs, nested case–control study, chemotherapy

items.title: Agent Sociodrama: Social-Dynamics-Guided Persona Recasting for LLM Agent Teams
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed as teams, yet they fail in characteristically social ways: information holders stay silent, dominant speakers anchor groups on wrong answers, and norm violations go unsanctioned. We present Agent Sociodrama, a framework for modeling and validating evolving social dynamics in LLM agent teams. Under fixed personas, agents' emotional states and directed, asymmetric relationships are updated every round by a unified external LLM judge and shape their subsequent interactions. Across six LLM backbones and five social scenarios, we assess social fidelity through classical social-theory patterns and agreement with human judgments. The resulting trajectories exhibit structured social patterns and model-specific differences. We then introduce Trajectory-Guided Persona Recasting (TPR), which diagnoses group-dynamic failures from interaction transcripts and social trajectories and recasts agent personas before rerunning the task. Across four collaborative benchmarks, TPR improves performance from both heterogeneous and randomly initialized agent persona compositions, yielding up to 83.3%p of accuracy improvement over the initial casting. On representative distributed-information cooperation and mixed-motive bargaining tasks, we outperform SOTOPIA and AgentVerse in three of four comparisons, by up to 37.5%p in Pareto rate. These results show that validated social trajectories provide actionable signals for repairing LLM agent teams.

items.title: Agent-assisted modeling for urban drainage systems
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to make water management more intuitive through natural language interfaces. However, the generalised training of these models limits their effectiveness at domain-specific tasks such as stormwater modelling, particularly when nuanced answers require executing and modifying water models. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) addresses this challenge by providing a standardised interface for LLMs to interact with external tools while enforcing guardrails for quality control. Building on this protocol, we introduce SWMM-MCP, a cross-platform, model agnostic framework that enables conversational interaction with the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s Stormwater Management Model (EPA SWMM). SWMM-MCP leverages the swmm_api and PySWMM libraries through an MCP server built with FAST-MCP, allowing users to configure, modify, and evaluate SWMM models via natural language. We demonstrate SWMM-MCP using a benchmark task and prompt-response evaluations comparing performance using eight different base LLMs. For the benchmark SWMM task, all base LLMs completed the tasks, but at varying levels of computational efficiency and detailed responses. For the prompt-response evaluations, the LLMs exhibited distinct personalities. Results highlight that even within a structured MCP framework, LLM selection significantly affects task efficiency and domain specific prompting remains important for optimal performance.

items.title: Agent-Canary-Mas: End-to-End Evaluation of Protocol Risk in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract: Agent-to-agent protocols allow LLM agents to discover peers, exchange results, and coordinate tool use. A locally successful protocol attack, however, may be rejected by a later agent or propagated into a consequential task decision. Measuring local exploitability alone leaves this difference unresolved and provides limited evidence about which participant caused the final outcome. We present Agent-Canary-Mas, an end-to-end evaluation system that follows protocol risk through long-horizon multi-agent tasks. It covers five risk classes and 13 subclasses across A2A, ANP, and BCS, with 975 matched malicious--benign task pairs in five business domains. A shared OpenClaw framework runs autonomous, tool-using agents under different underlying models while preserving the task and execution setup. Matched runs separate local protocol success from downstream consequences; retained evidence connects participant selection, message consumption, tool activity, and task-state changes. We further evaluate a protocol-context Guard that checks an object's authority at consequential handoffs. Across three model conditions, local attack success is frequently at or above 90%, while consequence conversion ranges from 7.1\% to 100.0\%. Cross-agent evidence raises macro-averaged Audit-F1 from 29.7% to 95.5%. On Finance tasks, the Guard lowers average ASR from 86.1% to 53.8% and PTCR from 65.5% to 31.2%, with a measurable completion tradeoff. These results show that protocol risk depends on how agents use exchanged objects throughout the task, and that evaluating this path supports more informative risk assessment, attribution, and defense.

items.title: AI ‐Powered Surveillance Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Technologies, Applications, Challenges, and Deployment Considerations
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed smart surveillance systems, significantly leveraging technologies such as deep learning, computer vision, and adaptive monitoring. Driven by the need for real‐time object detection, behavioral analysis, and automated alerting, AI‐powered surveillance is increasingly vital for enhancing public safety, operational efficiency, and decision‐making in fields such as security, health‐care, transportation, and environmental monitoring. The growing societal impact and complexity of surveillance necessitate a comprehensive examination of foundational methodologies, key application domains, and the technical, ethical, and operational challenges associated with these systems. Analysis reveals that although AI‐driven surveillance solutions offer improved accuracy, scalability, and responsiveness, they continue to face notable barriers including high computational demands, privacy and data quality concerns, interpretability limitations, and inadequate regulatory frameworks. The review further identifies critical emerging trends, such as sustainable AI practices, human‐AI collaborative models, and the integration of AI with the Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain technologies, as significant influences shaping the future trajectory of the field. Addressing these challenges through ongoing research, innovation, and responsible deployment is essential to fully unlock the societal and industrial potential of AI‐enabled surveillance solutions.

items.abstract: Mobile and application-derived artefacts are becoming more central to digital forensic investigations; however, they can be a diverse set of evidence in a UFDR which are hard to prioritize manually. Mobile and application derived-artifacts are becoming more important to digital forensic investigations, and can be a diverse set of evidence in a UFDR that is difficult to manually prioritize. In the paper, the authors propose an Artificial Intelligence-based UFDR report analysis and intelligent digital forensic investigation assistant to transform the extracted report information into a structured and explainable analysis flow. The prototype now supports reading reports in JSON, XML, CSV and ZIP formats, validates the uploaded report, calculates an integrity checksum (SHA-256), and stores proof of the integrity in SQLite. Twenty behavioral features are created in communication, temporal, browser, application, and file activity. The trained Random Forest (RF) classifier enables three-way classification, and a trained Isolation Forest (Anomaly scoring) is used. A suspicious detector based on the 4 parameters is set, and activates when late-night activity is detected, or when suspicious incoming/outgoing communication, suspicious text indicators or high anomaly scores are detected. items.title: AI-Driven Smart Haulage Technologies for Decarbonization and Sustainable Mine Transportation: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Haul trucks generate more than half of direct greenhouse-gas emissions in typical mining operations, making haulage decarbonization central to the industry’s net zero commitments. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to haulage, but existing reviews examine individual technologies rather than linking them to decarbonization and ESG outcomes. This comprehensive review synthesizes 73 peer-reviewed sources from 2017 to 2026 across route optimization, electric and hybrid trucks, predictive maintenance, fleet monitoring, carbon footprint reduction, and ESG performance, grades reported outcomes by validation basis, and develops a framework linking AI-enabled technology domains, through their operational mechanisms, to ESG outcomes. Reinforcement-learning dispatching reduced haulage emissions by more than 30% relative to fixed scheduling in simulation, trolley assist reduced fuel use by up to 91%, and fleet electrification modeling projected GHG reductions of up to 92.6% in a hypothetical case, contingent on grid carbon intensity. Most reported reductions derive from simulation, and AI’s advantage over conventional control of electrified fleets remains undemonstrated. Gaps include scarce field-verified emission baselines, limited modeling of operator behavior, immature cybersecurity and data governance practice, and weak engagement between ESG research and haulage technology. AI-enabled operational measures offer a promising near-term decarbonization pathway that complements, rather than awaits, fleet electrification.

items.title: AI-Guided Assignments in Practice: Students' Experiences in a Large Introductory Statistics Course
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) raise new questions for instructors, among them how to integrate LLMs productively into coursework and what to evaluate in students' work when an LLM can produce much of it directly. LLM-guided homework assignments offer one answer. Instructors configure the LLM to guide students in ways that achieve specific pedagogical goals, such as recalling material, discovering new concepts, or critically evaluating deliberately flawed reasoning, and grade the full student--LLM conversation, and with it the student's reasoning, rather than only the final answer. In this paper, we report on the large-scale deployment of such assignments, implemented through LLteacher, an open-source tool that supports recall, discovery, and critical-thinking assignments, in a large introductory statistics course serving mostly pre-major undergraduates. Results on 134 students show meaningful gains in self-reported confidence, with over 80\% agreeing that the assignments improved their comprehension of course material and their ability to interpret statistical results; gains were largest among students who started with lower confidence, suggesting this approach may help narrow gaps in preparation. Interaction patterns varied widely, from long single messages to rapid iterative exchanges, and hallucinations, when present, were rarely disruptive to learning.
